 <BODY BGCOLOR="WHITE" STYLE="line-height:Normal">

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="right"><B>Exhibit 99.1 </B></P> <P STYLE="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt" ALIGN="center">


<IMG SRC="g134020dsp5.jpg" ALT="LOGO">
 </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center">Atrium Therapeutics Doses First Patient in
Corventis<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP>, the First Interventional Clinical Trial for People Living with PRKAG2 Syndrome </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>&#8212; Global Phase 1/2 trial will evaluate ATR 1072 in approximately 37 participants &#8212; </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>&#8212; Initial proof of concept data expected in second half of 2027 &#8212; </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">SAN DIEGO, Oct. 27, 2026 &#8211; Atrium Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: RNA) (the &#8220;Company&#8221;), a biopharmaceutical company advancing precision
cardiology by developing RNA therapeutics targeted to the heart, today announced that the first patient has been dosed in the Phase 1/2 Corventis clinical trial evaluating ATR 1072, its lead investigational therapy for the potential treatment of
PRKAG2 (Protein Kinase <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">AMP-activated</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-catalytic</FONT> subunit Gamma 2) syndrome. The Company expects to report initial <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap"><FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">proof-of-concept</FONT></FONT> data from Corventis in the second half of 2027. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#8220;Dosing the first patient in the
Corventis clinical trial is a milestone for Atrium and, more importantly, for the PRKAG2 community. This is the first clinical trial for people living with PRKAG2 syndrome evaluating a potential treatment for the underlying cause of the disease. It
is also an important step for the broader genetic cardiomyopathy field as it moves toward treating these diseases at their root cause,&#8221; said Kathleen Gallagher, President and Chief Executive Officer of Atrium Therapeutics. &#8220;This
achievement reflects the dedication of our team and was made possible by our strong partnerships with our clinical trial sites and the support of the PRKAG2 syndrome patient community.&#8221; </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#8220;Today, the best we can offer people with PRKAG2 syndrome is a pacemaker, a defibrillator, and our best efforts to prevent life-threatening arrhythmias
&#8212; we manage the consequences of the disease, not the disease itself. Dosing the first patient with an investigational therapy designed to go after the genetic root cause is a real step forward for families affected by this rare genetic
cardiomyopathy,&#8221; said Michael Nassif, M.D., a heart failure cardiologist at Saint Luke&#8217;s Mid America Heart Institute. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">PRKAG2 syndrome is a
severe, life-threatening, rare autosomal dominant progressive cardiomyopathy with no approved therapies. It is caused by genetic mutations in PRKAG2 that lead to overactivity of <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">AMP-activated</FONT> protein kinase
(AMPK), resulting in glycogen accumulation in heart muscle, which may lead to heart failure and sudden cardiac death. ATR 1072, based on the Company&#8217;s targeted RNA delivery platform, is an antibody oligonucleotide conjugate (AOC) designed to
silence mutant PRKAG2 messenger RNA (mRNA) to normalize AMPK overactivation and improve heart function. </P>
</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt" ALIGN="center">


<IMG SRC="g134020dsp5.jpg" ALT="LOGO">
 </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About ATR 1072 </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">ATR
1072, the Company&#8217;s lead product candidate, is a potentially disease-modifying treatment for PRKAG2 syndrome. Using Atrium&#8217;s precision RNA delivery technology, ATR 1072 uses small interfering RNA (siRNA) to silence mutant PRKAG2
messenger RNA (mRNA), normalize <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">AMP-activated</FONT> protein kinase (AMPK) activity and reduce pathogenic glycogen accumulation, potentially leading to improved heart function. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About PRKAG2 Syndrome </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">PRKAG2 syndrome is a rare,
autosomal dominant, early-onset cardiomyopathy caused by mutations in the PRKAG2 gene, which encodes the Gamma 2 regulatory subunit of AMPK. Mutations enhance AMPK activity leading to abnormal glycogen accumulation in the heart, thickened heart
muscles, electrical conduction problems, and arrhythmias. Based on current scientific literature estimates, there are at least 1,000 &#8211; 2,000 people with PRKAG2 syndrome in the US. Current management is limited to symptomatic treatment; no
approved therapies exist to address the underlying genetic driver of disease. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About the
Corventis<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> Trial </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Corventis<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> is a
Phase 1/2 open-label, multicenter clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy of ATR 1072 in participants living with PRKAG2 syndrome. The study will enroll approximately 37
participants across two parts: Part A, multiple ascending dose cohorts to characterize safety and support dose selection, and Part B, a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">single-arm</FONT> expansion cohort at the recommended Phase 2 dose to further
evaluate efficacy trends in cardiac structure and function. The study&#8217;s primary endpoint is incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, with secondary and exploratory endpoints such as PRKAG2 mRNA reduction, siRNA tissue concentrations and
plasma pharmacokinetics. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Additional information about the trial is available at www.corventistrial.com. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About Atrium Therapeutics </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Atrium Therapeutics, Inc.
(Nasdaq: RNA) is pioneering targeted delivery of ribonucleic acid (RNA) therapeutics to the heart to transform the standard of care for people living with cardiomyopathies. The Company&#8217;s proprietary technology&#8212;designed at Avidity
Biosciences, Inc.&#8212;combines the tissue selectivity of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and other targeted delivery ligands with the precision of oligonucleotides and is designed to </P>
</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt" ALIGN="center">


<IMG SRC="g134020dsp5.jpg" ALT="LOGO">
 </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">selectively target the underlying drivers of genetically driven cardiac diseases through targeted, <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-viral</FONT> delivery of small interfering RNA (siRNA). This approach builds upon learnings from demonstrated delivery to skeletal muscle and applies it for efficient delivery to the heart, with the potential to
overcome challenges associated with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-specific</FONT> tissue delivery. The Company&#8217;s pipeline includes ATR 1072 for PRKAG2 syndrome, ATR 1086 for PLN (phospholamban) cardiomyopathy and two undisclosed
research targets in rare cardiomyopathies. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For more information about our RNA delivery platform, development pipeline and people, please
visit&nbsp;https://atriumtherapeutics.com/ and engage with us on&nbsp;LinkedIn. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Forward-Looking Statements </B></P>
